text.p01: To those who find their voice, just like Pip A Story about Courage and Finding Your Voice
text.p03: In the heart of a bright green jungle lived a young parrot named Pip.
text.p04: Every morning, the sun rose pink over the misty valley, and Pip woke up in his cozy home inside the oldest tree.
text.p05: His feathers were shiny, and his wings were strong.
text.p06: Pip's voice was small and quiet. He liked to hum to himself in the trees,
text.p07: but he never sang out loud when others were around.
text.p08: Other parrots chirped loudly from the treetops. Pip wanted to join, but his voice always shook.
text.p09: He remembered the times others laughed at how soft he sounded, so he chose to be silent.
text.p10: One afternoon, while flying quietly through the trees, Pip heard a strange sound: tiny chirps and soft cries.
text.p11: He followed the sound and found a baby bird that had fallen from its nest, calling for help.
text.p12: The nest was high, and the baby was too small to fly back up. Pip knew he had to do something.
text.p13: The little bird flapped its tiny wings and chirped in panic. Pip's heart pounded.
text.p14: He tried lifting the baby bird with his beak, but it was too heavy. He fluttered and struggled.
text.p15: But the baby just slid back onto the ground. Pip stepped back, thinking hard.
text.p16: “I need help,” he thought. “But that means I have to call out. Loudly.”
text.p17: Pip had always been afraid to use his voice, but now someone needed him.
text.p18: He took a deep breath, opened his wings wide, and sang the loudest song he had ever sung.
text.p19: His voice wobbled at first, but he kept going, louder and stronger, until the whole jungle was listening.
text.p20: Then the jungle grew quiet. Far away, wings fluttered.
text.p22: She swooped down and landed beside her baby.
text.p23: She looked at Pip and let out a soft, grateful chirp.
text.p24: Together, Pip and the mother bird carried the baby home.
text.p25: It wasn't easy, but Pip didn't stop. He felt strong, not in his wings, but in his heart.
text.p26: Back in the nest, the baby looked at Pip and sang a tiny version of his song.
text.p27: Pip's eyes widened. His song had helped, and now it was being passed on.
text.p28: From that day on, Pip sang whenever he felt happy or brave. Soon other birds were humming his tune.
text.p29: No one laughed anymore. They listened.
text.p30: Pip still remembered the days when he was afraid to speak.
text.p31: But now he knew: your voice doesn't have to be loud to be strong. It just has to be truly yours.
text.cover: Pip the Brave Parrot. A Story About Courage and Finding Your Voice
